- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of forecast to reduce noise.  
- In 30-day horizon, model often misses mean reversion; if price deviates >5% from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model delays correction; anticipate reversal 2–3 days ahead and adjust upward.
